title: Ordinary scalar perfect models compute local coefficient duals
statement: Let A be any commutative topological ring and let C_T be its canonical scalar realization on the pro-etale site [def-sfb-finite-constant-model-data]. Assume C_T is additive for each scheme T. Let S be a scheme, P an object of the unbounded derived category of modules over the continuous coefficient ring A_S [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and U_i -> S a pro-etale cover [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Suppose bounded complexes F_i of finite projective ordinary A-modules realize to P on each U_i. Let G_i be complexes equipped with isomorphisms tau_i^q: G_i^q -> Hom_A(F_i^(-q),A) such that d_G tau = tau (-(-1)^q d_F^*), for every pair of degrees. Then RHom(P,A_S) restricts on every original U_i to the realization of G_i. No assertion about scalar cohomology finiteness or global bounded constructibility is made.

proof.text: Transport internal abelian sheaf modules to sectionwise modules over the associated commutative ring sheaf. The constant-module and scalar-extension constructions identify the transported model with C_B(M)=B tensor underline M, naturally in M and linear maps. The ring map sends a to the constant section a.

Choose degreewise finite-free retract data for F. Apply scalarPerfectDualRealization and its ordinary comparison: internal Hom into the coefficient unit is computed by the scalar dual, with the differential -(-1)^q phi d_F. The supplied component isomorphisms tau identify G with this complex.

For every original covering member identify the covering slice with its pro-etale site, with its actual coefficient ring. Derived internal Hom commutes with this exact restriction. Apply the given local model isomorphism and the previous comparison and transport back to internal modules.
